newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds rise, but US holiday to dampen trade.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds rise, but US holiday to dampen trade.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose in early trade on Friday but activity was seen falling off later in the day as the US Independence Day holiday meant there would be no afternoon lead from Wall Street.
"There are not many sellers at these prices. The tendency is still upward but with the US closed it will put a damper on the (Danish) market this afternoon," a trader said.

He added that he expected the central bank to try and sell longer-dated bonds on Friday and could be expected shortly to start buying back 1998 paper, as it has said that it would. He expected buyers on Friday to focus on medium-term maturities.
On Thursday the central bank sold a total 1.3 billion crowns worth of the seven percent 2007, the five percent 2005, six percent 2002 and four percent 2000.
At 0745 GMT on Friday the tone-setting seven percent 2007 government bond, due officially to become the benchmark on September 1, was up 0.20 point, at 105.94 yielding 6.19 percent.
Its spread to the bund was unchanged at 60 basis points.
The outgoing benchmark eight percent 2006 bond was up to 113.26, yielding 5.99 percent.
The crown was virtually unchanged at 3.8076 to the mark. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 fell 0.07 point to 91.63.
